scores.rationale: The plan is a flat architecture catalogue with no phases, so no substrate-to-upper ordering or proven dependencies.
There is no Phase 0 or thin end-to-end production slice; everything is specified at once.

scores.evidence: Hybrid Approach: Database Per Tenant + Shared Services
scores.rationale: The tenancy choice is asserted with rationale but no default, flip condition or revisit trigger. The stack is listed as 'Node.js / Python / Go' with no decision made.
There are no phases, so there is no blast-radius ordering of work.
There is a detailed security section with middleware, but it is a standalone section, not tied to phases.

scores.evidence: Alerting thresholds: if (metrics.api_latency_p95 > 500) alert('API latency exceeds 500ms');
scores.rationale: Monitoring is described in detail but in standalone sections, not from a first phase onward.
CI/CD, Docker and npm ci are present but there are no phases, and there is no reproducible-data or environment story.
Idempotency keys, retries, dunning and blue-green deployment appear, but as a feature catalogue, not threaded across phases.
The plan never addresses whether an AI layer applies, and nothing declares it N/A.
Nothing is listed as deferred, and there are no pull-forward conditions. The plan claims it is 'production-ready'.

note: The plan is a broad, detailed design catalogue (schemas, code, security, CI/CD) with no phasing, no skeleton, no decision gates and no deferrals, so it scores very low against this rubric.
